issues: The copy relies on vague eco claims ('skip single-use plastic bottles') which this persona explicitly avoids, preferring specific sustainability metrics, supply chain transparency, or certifications.
The claim 'Designed to last' is unsupported by the stated claims, which do not mention the durability or materials of the containers.
The claims of being 'for less' and 'at a better value' are unsupported as there is no pricing or comparative value information in the stated claims.

config.advertiser_summary: An eco-friendly brand offering refillable, concentrated cleaning products designed to replace single-use plastic bottles with performance comparable to big brands.

assumptions: Price not given; assumed $60 for a 'unknown' product.
repeat_consumable: assumed 2.5 orders per customer over ~6 months.
Margin not given; assumed 55% (typical for home) for the break-even estimate only.
Break-even per customer (guidance, not enforced): $60 x 55% x 2.5 orders = $82.50.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click: verifiable without trusting a pixel. Maximise conversions within the budget: bids move between $0.25 and the $2.50 cap (category default) to spend it well; no CPA target is invented. Guidance: at the assumed margin, a click is worth about $0.99; bidding above that loses money per customer. Set a target CPA or a lower max CPC to enforce it.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: score 0.45, relative fit x1.40; 0.0096 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.75 (cap $2.50)
score 0.25, relative fit x1.04; 0.0096 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.31 (cap $1.87)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: fixed start bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: bid = start x pacing x conversion likelihood, within [floor, cap]: spend the budget on the best opportunities
phases.why: no CPA target was set, so the goal is the most units for the budget

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget, never above the $2.50 cap (category default).
